agentsMd: The three wording fixes read against the code: (a) 'a worker's claim keeps its locator, and the root's own claim — which never holds one — is skipped by the locator-less claim sweep when the root leg failed' ↔ retireTreeProcessesLocked's `!(rootOutcome === "failed" && token === architectToken)`, pinned by the StopFailed-at-linger test; (b) the log sentence ↔ the per-pass header at retireLingeringTrees, the per-tree line in retireTreeProcesses (when anything was retired), the per-tree failure line in retireLingeringTrees' catch, and the silent join (`if (inFlight) { await; return; }`); (c) 'Four paths change a lingering tree's record' ↔ beginLinger, reportRootExit → recordRootExit, the sweep, admit(). The /process/exit row and the closingTrees bullet match the new markProcessDead guard, the promoteWorkerQueue call, and the joined-close re-check. One nuance, not a defect: the documented format `root <stopped|failed|none>` can never print `failed` — a failed root leg sets anyFailed and the primitive throws StopFailed after its persist, so the `retired the processes of` line is only reached with `stopped` or `none`; the failure is reported by the caller's own line.
observations: A root whose stop failed keeps its claim record but its session capability was already revoked by the root leg before the stop attempt (`revokeRoleClaim` precedes `stopProcessSerialized`); what survives for the reopen is the claim's `sessionId` (the same-agent expectation), and the still-running root's next authenticated call 403s once and recovers through /worker-session as the reviewer's note describes.
